title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Efficiency of climate resilient agricultural production and marketing increased

Crop income of project farmers increased by 30% Progress/Status: In 2020, PIU conducted the baseline survey in some of the project's target soums. Per the survey results, the average crop income of farmers is MNT922,580 in a year. Irrigation systems are not yet operational. of 30 June 2025.
As of 30 September 2025, 6 irrigation systems have been commissioned, but none are operational due to delayed development of O&M arrangements and procedures. Hence, no progress has been made in achieving this outcome indicator.
As of Q4 2025, 157 farmers harvested 241 tons of vegetables, 1,094 tons of potatoes, and 49.3 tons of green fodder, generating MNT 1.7 billion in total income. The average income per participant was approximately MNT 10.8 million, significantly higher than anticipated due to the actual number of farmers being far below the target of 3,548 farmers. Data Source: Sample household survey, agriculture survey and statistical yearbook Actual value:

Land with higher productivity increased to 7,000 hectares Progress/Status: In 2021 and early 2022, the EA awarded 10 contracts for upgrading irrigation schemes across several aimags and soums, covering a total of 3,031 hectares (ha). 4 Irrigation systems ((i) Tsul Ulaan in Bayannuur, Bayan-Ulgii, (ii) Iven Gol in Sant, Selenge, (iii) Sugnugur in Batsumber, Tuv, and (iv) Yolton in Khaliun, Gobi-Altai) were commissioned by the technical and state commissions by June 2025. A total 861 ha irrigation system was completed by 30 June 2025.
Q3 2025: Six irrigation systems covering 2,028 ha have been commissioned, but none are operational due to delayed development of O&M arrangements and procedures. Hence, no progress has been made in achieving this outcome indicator. Hence, no progress has been made in achieving this outcome indicator.
Q4 2025: progress 29.4% • Completed: 2,061 ha (7 IS) • Ongoing for completion in 2026: 970 ha (3 IS) • To be upgraded in 2026-2027: 1,782 ha (5 IS) Total: 4,813 ha at 16 IS Data Source: Sample household survey, agriculture survey and statistical yearbook Actual value:

Vegetable and potato crop yields for project farmers increased by about 30% and 15%, respectively Progress/Status: According to the baseline survey results, an average vegetable yield is 8.1 t/ha and potato yield is estimated as 11.7 t/ha.
Q3 2025: Irrigation systems are not yet operational. Hence, no progress has been made in achieving this outcome indicator.
Q4 2025: 8% for vegetable crop yields and 34% for potato crop yields. Data Source: Sample household survey, agriculture survey and statistical yearbook Actual value:

Number of vegetable farmers benefitting from access to climate-smart production support increased to 3,548 Progress/Status: Per the baseline survey results conducted in 2020, there were 266 vegetable farmers, producing potato and other vegetable, under the target irrigation schemes fields.
Q3 2025: Irrigation systems are not yet operational. Hence, no progress has been made in achieving this outcome indicator.
Q4 2025: 157 farmers accessed improved IS to grow vegetables. Data Source: Sample household survey, agriculture survey and statistical yearbook Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: 100% of contracts/ documents for 3,094 households engaged in vegetable farming in new plots are co-signed by women Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 0%. Allocation of new plots at improved irrigations systems to households engaged in vegetable farming has not started yet, pending the finalization of operational plans for irrigation schemes by the CS-29 consultants. Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: 240 locals including 40% women and 10% from female headed households hired during construction Achievement: 12.5 Progress/Status: Q4 2025: 413 locals (or 172% of target), were hired during construction work, including 113 or 22% women, of which 27 or 8% female headed households.
Before Q2 2025: The requirements and criteria to comply with the measures outlined in the GAP and SDAP—specifically, hiring local workers with a target of 40% women and 10% female headed households during construction—were incorporated into the civil works bidding documents and construction work programs. The civil works contractors committed to hiring local community members, including women and female household heads, and reflected these commitments in their respective work plans. Since the commencement of civil works for the irrigation schemes in 2022, a total of 346 local workers have been employed across the construction of 10 irrigation schemes. Of these, 76 workers (22%) were women, and 27 workers (8%) were female heads of households. Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: At least 20 hectares of drip/ precision irrigation systems installed and operational in each irrigation scheme financed by JFPR grant Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 0% • Completed in 2025: 2 ha (1 IS) • To be completed by 2027: 100 ha (10 IS)
Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Environmentally sustainable agriculture production systems improved Indicator: 192 women from CGGs received training on best practices for food safety Progress/Status: PIU developed a “Public campaign plan for 2020-2026”, including training and information dissemination plan that was approved by the Project director. The training plan includes the female-focused training sessions. No progress has been made as of 30 September 2025.
Q4 2025: Progress: 66,1% A total of 127 women from CGGs received training on good agricultural practices and food safety, including harvesting techniques and root cellar disinfection. The training was delivered by the CS-13 vegetable production facilitation firm.
Data Source: Quarterly progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Environmentally sustainable agriculture production systems improved Indicator: 20 women researchers received technical support on pest management Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 0% Pesticide testing equipment and reagents to IPP under target 2b have not been procured, hence no training was conducted. Data Source: Quarterly progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Environmentally sustainable agriculture production systems improved Indicator: 3,548 farmers including 50% women receive high-yielding and climate-resilient vegetable seeds Achievement: 381 Progress/Status: No progress has been made as of 31 December 2025, as the CRIS have not yet started producing high yield seeds. Data Source: Quarterly progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports

Output: Technical, institutional, and management capacity and coordination strengthened Indicator: With ADB loan support: 24 winter greenhouses and collective cold storage facilities in use by CGGs Progress/Status: The EA has initiated the procurement of greenhouses and storage facilities for CGGs for advertisement in Q1 2024. No progress has been made as of 30 June 2025.
Q4 2025: Progress; 0% The EA proposed to procure 2 greenhouses for 1,000 m2 each with JFPR grant financing. On 19 December 2025, the PSC resolved to procure 10 collective cellars with a 100-ton capacity each in 2026.
Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Technical, institutional, and management capacity and coordination strengthened Indicator: With ADB loan support: At least 144 persons report improved skills technical and management issues conducted for soum and bagh local authorities, of which at least 30% are women Achievement: 93 Progress/Status: There have the Soum Working Group established in the project target 12 soums, where the irrigation schemes are to be constructed. The PIU has conducted “The Project Implementation status and Safeguard, EMP and Gender Policy Introductory online training” were conducted for 6 soum SWGs, CDC, 3 Consultant team and CW contractors from April 10 to May 7, 2025. Total of 45 government specialists and SWGs, CDC engineers, consultant firm members and CW contractors participated in the online training sessions. 22% or 10 were women participants.
Q4 2025: Progress: • 195% or cumulatively 282 persons • including 64.2% or 181 female participants.
Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports

Output: Technical, institutional, and management capacity and coordination strengthened Indicator: With JFPR grant support: At least 48 CGGs established, have an agreed operational plan and are producing vegetables and potatoes, with at least 40% women as members and 25% in leadership positions Achievement: 36 Progress/Status: Vegetable Production Facilitation consulting firm (Package C13) supports the EA/IAs in forming the CGGs, promoting greenhouse vegetable production, vegetable processing, and marketing, formulation of capacity development plans and their implementation, water management, and use of sprinkler irrigation equipment. The team conducted a preliminary assessment of the situation in the project soums and organized discussions with community members and vegetable growers on establishing vegetable grower cooperatives or CGGs, encouraging their participation and proactiveness in achieving the project goals by cooperation, better resource utilization, business planning, and other mutually beneficial activities and initiatives. Coordinators in 11 soums have been appointed. As of date, the consulting firm assisted in the establishment of 59 CGGs/cooperatives with 810 members in 10 soums of 7 provinces. 30,9%, or 251 of the total members are women; 10% or 82 members are female heads of household; and 11,6%, or 94 members, are from poor families. And 30,5% or 18 groups have female leaders, as of 30 June 2025.
Q4 2025: Progress: • 122% or 59 CGGs have been established. • 33.7% or 273 of the 810 CGG members are women. • 6.5% or 18 female members of CGGs are in leadership positions.
Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports

Output: Technical, institutional, and management capacity and coordination strengthened Indicator: With JFPR grant support: At least 480 persons report At least 480 persons report improved skills on climate-smart farming and irrigation technologies provided to CGGs of which at least 40% are women Progress/Status: Vegetable Production Facilitation consulting firm (Package C13) has been developing the capacity building programs for soum governments and CGGs. 16 times of online, classroom and field trainings were conducted under 7 main topics (Greenhouse vegetable cultivation, Irrigated agricultural technology, Keeping soil fertility methods, Growing animal fodder, Irrigation scheme field training) were conducted by the consulting firm. 788 CGG members and local government specialists involved in the training. 338 or 49.2% were women out of the 788 farmers of CGGs in 2024. As of 30 June 2025, 445 CGG members participated in the vegetable cultivation training, Good agriculture practice, greenhouse farming, seed and fertilizer training.
Q4 2025: Progress: • 252% or cumulatively 1,214 persons have been trained • including 43,7% or 783 women.
Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Environmentally sustainable agriculture production systems improved Indicator: IPP conducting 5,000 tests of vegetables and pesticides for food safety Progress/Status: The project has not started the procurement of any goods, works and consulting services to support this activity. In December 2024, three irrigation systems of Crop Production Research Institutes were selected for rehabilitation. This output depends on completion the civil works for such rehabilitation. No progress has been made as of 31 December 2025. Data Source: Quarterly progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: Irrigation and drainage infrastructure upgraded and modernized to service at least 7,000 ha of farmland Achievement: 2028 Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 29.4% with 2,061 ha of irrigated farmland completed. • Completed: 861 ha in 2024 and 1,200 ha in 2025 (7 IS) • Ongoing for completion in 2026: 970 ha (3 IS) • To be upgraded in 2026-2027: 1,782 ha (6 IS)
Q3 2025: As of 30 September 2025, six out of ten irrigation systems—covering 2,028 hectares out of a total 3,031 hectares—have been completed and commissioned. However, none are currently operational due to delays in developing the operations and management arrangements and procedures.
As of 30 June 2025, the civil works for rehabilitation of 4 irrigation schemes covering 861 ha was commissioned. out of total 10 contracted irrigations systems covering 3,031 ha of farmland.
In December 2024, the EA identified four new sites for rehabilitation of irrigation systems. Two consulting services packages for EBA and DEIA and DED for Bornuur Irrigation scheme (CS34), Erdene-Uul and Khongor-Ovoo Irrigation schemes (CS35) have been contracted. Khongor Ovoo is replaced with 79 irrigation scheme via amendment to the contract. Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports
ADB review mission reports

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: All project soums ensure O&M of project supported irrigation schemes Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 0% Although seven irrigation systems were state commissioned, as of 31 December 2025, none have been made operational. Cooperation agreements have been signed between MOFALI and aimag and soum governments for all 10 irrigation schemes, but the O&M arrangements for each subproject are yet to be finalized, agreed upon with soums and end-users, and made operational. Transfer of assets from MOFALI to the aimags for registration and ownership and, subsequently to the soums for operation, has been delayed.
Q3 2025: The Soum Working Groupd (SWG) was established in the project target 10 soums, where the irrigation schemes are to be constructed. Consulting firm for capacity building in the use, operations and maintenance of irrigation systems was contracted in April 2025. The consulting firm has been developing O&M procedures for each irrigation system. These will be finalized in consultation with the MOFALI, (PIU), local governments, and community grower groups. MOFALI has signed agreements with the respective aimag and soum governments on ownership and O&M of irrigation schemes. Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
ADB review mission reports

Output: Efficient and climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and management systems installed Indicator: Pilot irrigation asset management systems commissioned in one project soums in the Western Region and one in the Central or Eastern Region Progress/Status: Q4 2025: Progress: 0% Capacity building consulting firm (CS-29) was mobilized in April 2025 and will develop and pilot asset management system at Yolton IS (Gobi-Altai, Khaliun soum, western region) and Sugnugur (Tuv, Batsumber-central region) in 2026.
Q3 2025: Vegetable production consulting firm and Capacity building for use of the irrigation system consulting firm will pilot a modern asset management system at the commissioned irrigation schemes namely, CW-8-1 Iven Gol (Sant, Selenge) and CW-8-2 Sugnugur(Batsumber, Tuv) from May to October 2025. Data Source: Semi-annual progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU

Output: Environmentally sustainable agriculture production systems improved Indicator: Four crop production research institutes producing 1.8 tons of vegetable seeds and 40 tons of seed potatoes Progress/Status: In 2024, the EA's project steering committee finalized the list of Crop Production Research Institutes to be supported under the project. There is no progress made in procuring civil works. The goods package G-05: Seed research equipment for research laboratory in central region (Darkhan Elite Farm) was contracted in April 2025.
Q4 2025: Progress: 0% Civil works to upgrade IS at CPRIs have not been procured due to multiple changes in the selection of CPRIs to be supported, and most recently, due to unsuccessful first bidding process in December 2025. Consequently, the project has not been able to provide any support for seed production. Rebidding is scheduled for Q1 2026. Data Source: Quarterly progress/ implementation reports produced by PIU
